epics.title: Retire oversized provider sessions across runner restarts
epics.objective: Bound turn cost and checkpoint growth by retiring a persistent provider session on its next resume once its observed context crosses a global cap, and reclaim DeepAgents checkpoint state through a provider-neutral release port.

tasks.title: Measurement, storage, and the quality gate
tasks.objective: Give every persistent provider session a typed context high-water mark and the fenced repository operations that raise and retire it, teach both adapters to report model-visible input (including on error frames) with explicit per-route cache semantics, make resetScope return the references it removes, and put npm run lint under verify and CI. After this task the host can measure and retire, but no policy fires yet.
acceptance_criteria: S1 derivation: modelVisibleInputTokens returns 271,500 for an Anthropic usage of 1,000 input / 270,000 cache read / 500 cache write; 1,000 for an OpenAI-compatible usage of 1,000 input / 800 cached; the additive form for a mixed or unresolved route; totalBillableInputTokens and all other billing fields unchanged; the route resolves from usage.modelRoute and falls back to usage.provider when modelRoute is absent (provider fallback).

S2/R2 partial usage, spawned runners: an errored Claude worker run and an errored DeepAgents worker run each write one cumulative partial-usage payload with the turn's usageEventId on their single error frame; Claude carries it as a typed QueryFailure thrown from the result branch and written by runner/index.ts; DeepAgents carries it as a typed DeepAgentPartialUsage value passed stream-normalizer → deep-agent-runner → index.

S2/R2 partial usage, inline lanes: an errored Claude inline-lane turn and an errored DeepAgents inline-lane turn each emit one terminal error output carrying the accumulated usage with the turn's usageEventId.

S3 storage: provider_sessions.context_high_water_mark is a nullable integer column added by a generated drizzle migration (db:migrations:check clean); raiseProviderSessionContextHighWaterMark keeps the larger value, leaves metadata_json untouched, rejects a stale owner, ignores non-resumable rows, rejects non-integer or negative values before SQL with ProviderSessionMeasurementError, and returns whether a row changed; the turn-context projection returns contextHighWaterMark.

R1 fences: raise and retireProviderSession compare agent_sessions.reset_at with IS NOT DISTINCT FROM the caller's generation; a null/null generation succeeds and null versus non-null is rejected on both operations.

R1 retirement: retireProviderSession is one atomic active→expired UPDATE fenced on id, agent_session_id, provider, external_session_id, status='active' and the generation, returning { providerSessionId, externalSessionId, executionProviderId } or undefined; the fingerprint-change, missing-session and ops-service facade callers switch to it, while the compaction-delta degradation path keeps the existing expireProviderSession helper unchanged (0159 §4).

R3 registry: every executable route's cacheSupport.prompt declares cacheReadsIncludedInInput and cacheWritesIncludedInInput (type in model-provider-registry.ts); the registry validator fails a route missing either; nonzero OpenAI and OpenRouter cache-write usage yields inputTokens unchanged; DeepAgents normalised usage carries the resolved provider and modelRoute.

R4 return type: resetScope returns an immutable list of retired { providerSessionId, externalSessionId, executionProviderId } selected FOR UPDATE before delete and returned after commit, and a readonly empty list on no-route or empty paths; canonical-session-ops-service, canonical-ops-repo.postgres.ts and clearSessionForChatJid propagate it; no caller releases yet.

S11 lint gate: a package.json script lint:changed (ESLint over the TypeScript files changed against the merge-base with origin/main) runs inside FACTORY_STRUCTURAL_CMD in .envrc and as the blocking CI check step; full npm run lint stays an advisory continue-on-error CI step; every file this task touches is lint-clean; the 82 pre-existing errors outside the diff are recorded as deferral D-0080 with a trigger and are neither fixed, baselined nor suppressed here.

S10 unchanged behaviour: the four pinned tests (group-processing 'passes hydrated memory context with provider session resume id', agent-runner-ipc 'resumes and persists SDK sessions for live channel turns', claude-agent-sdk-boundary 'passes hermetic Gantry capabilities and settings into the Claude SDK', deepagents-memory-context 'injects the trust-scoped memory block exactly once as a model-visible user message') and the scheduled-job tests are untouched and green; python3 factory/scripts/verify.py is green.

tasks.reviewer_focus: Load-bearing constitution references: pnp-coding-standards-modular-monolith.md (domain error types, no bare Error; typed constants over string literals; mappers separate from data access) and 03-modular-monolith-structure.md (adapter-owned provider knowledge stays in adapters; domain/repositories owns the port). Task-specific seam: the two new repository operations are single SQL statements whose predicates are the whole safety story — the null-safe reset_at fence must appear in BOTH raise and retire, and retire must be the only path that flips active→expired and must RETURN the row it flipped; the compaction-delta degradation path is deliberately left on the old expire helper (ready row) and must not be 'cleaned up' into retire. Concerns that must not share a file: measurement value validation and its domain error (domain/sessions), the SQL (repository helpers), the derivation (shared/model-usage), the registry booleans and their validator (provider registry). Partial-usage carriers are typed value objects: DeepAgents threads DeepAgentPartialUsage through three runner files; Claude throws a typed QueryFailure that runner/index.ts unwraps into exactly one error frame — never two frames, never ad-hoc fields on Error. Inline lanes mirror the same shape in their own modules. resetScope's return is readonly and never undefined. The migration is generated by drizzle-kit and committed as emitted. Deferred to T2 with TODO(T2): reading the mark for policy and raising it after runs — T1 only exposes the operations and the projection; deferred to T3: consuming the retired references.

tasks.title: Host policy, cap setting, events, and docs
tasks.objective: Make the ceiling fire: read the global cap from a revisioned setting, retire an over-cap session at preflight through the T1 operations with a non-hydrating lost-race re-read, raise the mark after every measured run, publish the two retirement events directly and best-effort, and record the operator procedures, the executed observability recipe, and the architecture alignment. T2 also owns the retirement release queue and its single post-reply drain call in group-agent-runner.ts and registers BOTH new event types (session.provider.retired, session.provider.cleanup_failed) so T3 never edits the runner or the event registry.
acceptance_criteria: S4: a usage-bearing errored run raises the mark; a run with no measurement does not call the raise operation.

S5: an over-cap active session is not passed as the resume id; retirement returns the reference; the run proceeds fresh; the replacement handle is persisted; the reply is delivered; a crossing run is retired on the following resume; a maintenance_compact row is not retired; a ready row is promoted first; a lost transition persists no replacement.
R6: the lost-race re-read uses hydrateMemory: false and reuses the hydrated block when the agent session id and null-normalised generation match.
S6: an under-cap or unmarked session resumes with the memory block and the snapshot; the four pinned tests stay green and untouched.

S7: limits.provider_session_max_input_tokens parses beside provider entries, defaults to 150,000, rejects values outside 20,000–900,000 with a path-level error, round-trips through the revision document and export, is applied from a new revision, and a worker below reader version 16 holds its prior revision and alerts.

S9/R5: session.provider.retired and session.provider.cleanup_failed are registered event types with typed payloads, published directly by the host with appId, actor, sessionId (and runId for missing-session), best-effort so publication failure never suppresses the reply, with publish, query and projection tests.

S12/R7: docs/memory/provider-session-ceiling-operations.md holds the pre-deploy reset with its stop condition, the orphan scan, and the observability SQL, which a Postgres test executes; runtime-components.md and canonical-domain-model.md no longer say fresh runs restore memory only.
S10/S11: scheduled-job tests untouched and green; verify.py green.

Parallel seam: group-agent-runner.ts carries a typed release queue (retired references collected from ceiling, fingerprint and missing-session retirement) drained exactly once after the turn's final reply through a host function releaseRetiredProviderSessions(refs) that T2 stubs as a no-op with TODO(T3); both event types are registered and typed in T2; T3 does not touch group-agent-runner.ts or runtime-event-types.ts.

tasks.title: Adapter release port and post-reply coordinator
tasks.objective: Reclaim DeepAgents checkpoint state for retired sessions: add releaseSession to the adapter contract, implement it in the DeepAgents adapter with deleteThread, and add the host coordinator that runs after the reply for ceiling, fingerprint, missing-session and both /new paths, sanitising errors and publishing cleanup_failed. Runs in parallel with T2 (graph amendment approved by Ravi in chat, 2026-09-09): T3 implements releaseRetiredProviderSessions in a new runtime module plus the adapter port and both /new handlers, consuming T1's retired-reference type; it never edits group-agent-runner.ts or runtime-event-types.ts, which T2 owns.
acceptance_criteria: S8: for ceiling, missing-session, fingerprint and /new, the retired thread's rows leave checkpoints, checkpoint_blobs and checkpoint_writes; checkpoint_migrations and other threads' rows remain; a second call is a no-op; a simulated deletion failure leaves the session expired, the reply delivered and session.provider.cleanup_failed recorded; a lost retirement transition performs no cleanup.
R4 (wiring): both /new handlers (session-commands.ts idle path and runtime-services-active-new.ts active path) send their reply, then release each returned reference.
R5 (sanitiser): the cleanup_failed error contains no external session id, thread id or connection string.
Release never runs before the turn's final reply path has unblocked; the coordinator resolves the adapter by executionProviderId and the Claude adapter is a no-op.
S10/S11: scheduled-job tests untouched and green; verify.py green.

Parallel seam: T3's write scope is disjoint from T2's — adapter contract, DeepAgents adapter and checkpoint setup, the new provider-session-release.ts coordinator exporting releaseRetiredProviderSessions(refs), session-commands.ts and runtime-services-active-new.ts /new handlers, and tests; the cleanup_failed publication uses the event type T2 registers and integrates at merge.
